item.title: Ocean Expo Park — Guide
item.description: Ocean Expo Park (Ocean Expo Commemorative National Government Park), on the Motobu Peninsula in northern Okinawa, is a vast seaside park built for the 1975 International Ocean Exposition and one of the island’s top family destinations. While its most famous attraction is the world-class Churaumi Aquarium, the park offers far more across its expansive, beautifully landscaped grounds. Highlights include free dolphin shows at the Okichan Theater, the Dolphin Lagoon, a Manatee and Sea Turtle pool, the Tropical Dream Center with orchids and greenhouses, the Oceanic Culture Museum and planetarium, the reconstructed Okinawan village of Omoro Arboretum, and the lovely Emerald Beach for swimming.

item.title: Saga Castle Ruins and History Hall — Guide
item.description: Saga Castle, in the centre of Saga city, was the seat of the Nabeshima clan who ruled the domain through the Edo period. Though the main keep is long gone, the site preserves impressive relics — a broad moat, earthen ramparts, and the imposing Shachi-no-mon gate — set in a pleasant park famous for cherry blossom in spring. The highlight is the Saga Castle History Museum (Honmaru History Hall), a magnificent and faithful reconstruction of the castle’s original wooden palace, one of the largest wooden reconstructions in Japan.

item.title: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — Guide
item.description: Shinjuku Gyoen is one of Tokyo’s largest and most beautiful gardens, a tranquil green oasis of over 58 hectares set right beside the skyscrapers and bustle of Shinjuku. Originally a feudal lord’s residence and later an imperial garden, it opened to the public after the war. Its special charm lies in combining three distinct landscape styles in one park: a spacious, manicured French formal garden with symmetrical flowerbeds and plane-tree avenues; a wide, rolling English landscape garden of open lawns and mature trees; and a classical Japanese garden with ponds, bridges, islands and a traditional teahouse.

item.title: Tokushima Castle Ruins and Mount Bizan — Guide
item.description: Tokushima city grew up around Tokushima Castle, built in the late sixteenth century by the ruling Hachisuka clan at the foot of Mount Bizan. Though the castle buildings are gone, the site is now a pleasant park preserving impressive stone walls and moats, along with the beautiful Senshukaku Japanese landscape garden, a nationally designated scenic spot. Rising directly behind it is Mount Bizan, the symbol of the city, whose summit is reached by a ropeway or a road and rewards you with a sweeping panorama over Tokushima, the Yoshino River delta and the Seto Inland Sea — especially fine at night.

item.title: Yoyogi Park — Guide
item.description: Yoyogi Park, next to Harajuku and the Meiji Shrine forest, is one of Tokyo’s largest and most popular parks, and a wonderful place to see everyday Tokyo life at play. Once an Olympic Village site for the 1964 Games, it’s now a broad, open expanse of spacious lawns, wooded groves, ponds and fountains, hugely popular on weekends when locals come to picnic, jog, cycle, practise music and dance, walk their dogs and simply relax.

item.title: Osaka Castle Guide: The Tower, Park & Best Times to Visit
item.description: Rising on its great stone base above a sea of green, Osaka Castle is the symbol of the city and its single most famous sight. The gleaming white-and-green keep, trimmed with golden tigers and crests, sits within a vast park ringed by massive stone walls and broad moats — a monument to Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the warlord who unified Japan and built his power base here in the 16th century. Today the keep houses a modern museum, the top floor offers sweeping city views, and the surrounding park is one of Osaka’s best spots for cherry and plum blossom.
